summary: A quiet weekend for competitors. Lasso, URLgenius, Button/Posttap and Amazon's tools had no real news (LinkedIn was rate-limited for Lasso, so its LinkedIn page wasn't checked).
YouTube Shopping keeps growing its affiliate programme in India, adding Amazon, AJIO, Meesho, Snapdeal and Tata CLiQ, with over 19 million videos tagged since launch.
Lnk.Bio is pitching itself as a workaround for Facebook's test that limits some Pages to two link posts a month unless they pay for Meta One.

items.title: YouTube wants a share of India's shopping carts. Will ad budgets follow?
items.why: YouTube's affiliate programme in India now covers Amazon, Flipkart, Myntra, Nykaa and more. YouTube says over half of eligible Indian creators had enrolled by May and payouts grew more than 160% year on year. More of the path from a creator's video to a store now runs through the platform's own built-in affiliate links.

items.title: Facebook is limiting some Pages to just 2 posts with links per month unless you upgrade to Meta One. Workaround: add LnkBio to your Page
items.why: Link-in-bio tools are using Meta's paid link limits as a sales pitch. Meta's own rules exempt links to its apps, ads, and product and affiliate links in a business's Meta catalogue, so links that go off Meta are the ones being squeezed.
